subject: pe

moments.title: IOC founded at the Sorbonne
moments.body: On 23 June 1894, Coubertin convenes the International Athletic Congress at the Sorbonne. Delegates from 9 countries agree to revive the Olympic Games. The International Olympic Committee is formed. Coubertin, inspired by Thomas Arnold's Rugby School and the Wenlock Olympian Games (Shropshire, since 1850), saw sport as moral education.
moments.takeaway: The modern Olympic movement was created by a French aristocrat inspired by English public-school muscular Christianity.

moments.title: Jesse Owens at Berlin
moments.body: African American sprinter Jesse Owens wins four gold medals (100m, 200m, long jump, 4x100m relay) at the Nazi-hosted Berlin Olympics. Hitler had hoped the Games would demonstrate Aryan supremacy. Owens befriends German long jumper Luz Long, who advised him on his approach run after a foul. Owens was famously not snubbed by Hitler — but was largely ignored by President Roosevelt back home.

quote.text: Hitler didn't snub me — it was [our president] who snubbed me. The president didn't even send me a telegram.

moments.takeaway: An African American athlete demolished Nazi racial ideology in front of Hitler, then returned to a segregated America.

now.title: Olympic movement today
now.body: The IOC governs the Summer and Winter Olympics, with revenues over $7bn per 4-year cycle. Recent Games (Tokyo 2020, Beijing 2022, Paris 2024) have grappled with cost, climate, and athlete welfare. The 'Olympic Truce' is regularly invoked; geopolitical tensions (Russia, Israel) increasingly test it.
now.open_questions: How can the Games be hosted without bankrupting cities? LA 2028 and Brisbane 2032 use mostly existing venues.

reflection: Coubertin's vision was explicitly elitist and male-only ('The Olympic Games... with the solemn and periodic exaltation of male athleticism, with internationalism as a base...'). Every later opening of the Games to women, Black athletes, professionals and Para-athletes was a fight against his founding intent.
